subject.title: Cron Jobs Calendar View for Control UI

question: Should maintainers accept a current-page 24-hour cron timeline as the first product slice, require a fuller day/week/calendar design first, or defer the feature?
rationale: The request is a user-visible Control UI feature rather than a broken existing contract, and the open implementation PR only covers part of the requested scope while needing a substantial rebase.

options.title: Request a fresh/rebased timeline slice
options.body: Ask for a current-main implementation of the 24-hour timeline first, using existing scheduler/status contracts and leaving day/week/drag scope for follow-up decisions.

options.title: Design the full calendar scope first
options.body: Pause implementation until maintainers define daily, weekly, stats, validation, and drag-to-reschedule behavior as one product design.

options.title: Defer the calendar view
options.body: Keep the existing list/run-history UI and close or park the implementation PR if maintainers do not want this in core now.

recommendation.title: Request a fresh/rebased timeline slice
recommendation.body: Ask for a current-main implementation of the 24-hour timeline first, using existing scheduler/status contracts and leaving day/week/drag scope for follow-up decisions.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest historical ownership signal across the Control UI cron surface and product-scope review context.
